parsed.title: TCP and UDP
summary_points: TCP is connection-oriented, uses a three-way handshake, and guarantees reliable, in-order delivery.
TCP provides flow control, congestion control, and is used for HTTP, email, and FTP.
UDP is connectionless with no handshake, no delivery guarantees, and a small 8-byte header.
UDP is faster and has lower latency, making it ideal for DNS, streaming, gaming, and VoIP.
parsed.one_line: TCP offers reliable and ordered delivery, while UDP prioritizes speed and low latency.
